title: Scan student text for contradictions
statement: Scan every line a student reads for internal contradictions: mismatched counts, one term used two ways, directions that don't fit the interaction, and references to things not on the page.
example: One modelled step said it took the "two strongest" and then wrote one quote.
detail: Review rounds on a Grade 3 course found lines that contradicted themselves: a modelled step said "two strongest" but wrote one quote (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0223-g3-review-rounds-and-tooling-2026-09-18-to-21.qmd`), and a word card set "three parts" against "two meaningful parts". A scan then walked 3,003 child-facing strings across four lessons, hunting by pattern for number words that don't fit their nouns, one term with two meanings, instructions that don't fit the interaction, references to things off the page, and rubric counts that don't match their lists (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0238-l4-baseline-submission-and-signoff-packet-2026-08-31.qmd`). Its 95 raw hits all triaged clean, for 0 live contradictions.
against: The scan has only guarded so far: it found 0 live contradictions, and the word-card case was fixed before it ran, so every contradiction on record was found by people reading the lessons (the same two files).
